c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the Victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

Part Eleven
Child-Friendly District Development Policy

Article 29
(1) Regional Apparatus with authority over Women and Children shall formulate service policy regarding the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence.
(2) The formulation of service policy as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented through the following mechanism:
a. formulating case reporting policy related to Women and Children who become Victims of acts of Violence;
b. preparing reporting and referral mechanisms between regional apparatus organizations with authority over the protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence with relevant agencies and with P2TP2A; and
c. preparing budget for the implementation of protection policy for Women and Children against acts of Violence.

Article 15
(1) Regional Government is obligated to:
a. implement policies for the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence established by the government;
b. establish policies, programs, and activities for the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence; and
c. conduct cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, as well as educational institutions, health institutions, hospitals, and various NGOs concerned with Women and Children in the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence.
(2) Regional Government is responsible for providing support for facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence.
(3) In order to carry out the obligations as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, Regional Government establishes action programs and activities for the protection of Women and Children in 1 (one) Regional Action Plan as a basis for regional apparatus in implementing protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.
(4) Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (3), constitutes part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD).
(5) Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (3), is further regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is South Labuhanbatu Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of South Labuhanbatu.
4. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life, both individual and collective, in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
5. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering, whether physical, sexual, psychological, and/or domestic neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old, including a Child who is still in the womb.
7. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
8. Violence against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against Children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of Children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
10. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences violence and/or threat of violence.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from acts of Violence and discrimination.
13. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy, integrated for the strengthening and recovery of Violence Victims.
15. Gender is the difference in characteristics, roles, functions and status between Women and men that is not based on biological differences, but rather based on socio-cultural relations influenced by the broader structure of society.
16. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate Gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region.
17. Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter abbreviated as Dinas PPPA, is the office that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
18. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated Service center in the effort to empower Women and Children established by the Regional Government with active participation of the Community, which includes an information center, consultation center, complaint service, initial health care, counseling, legal assistance, repatriation and social reintegration, shelter/temporary safe house (shelter), and referral center.
19. Safe House is a shelter/temporary protection house for Victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of Victims from threats and danger from perpetrators, and is only known to interested parties such as certain personnel at UPT P2TP2A for reasons of Victim safety and security.
20. Standard Operating Procedure, hereinafter abbreviated as SOP, is the standard steps that must be taken in protecting Victims starting from complaint/identification, rehabilitation, health, Social Rehabilitation, advocacy up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or Victims.
21. Family is the smallest unit in the Community consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child or blood Family in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree and/or if any up to the fourth degree.
22. Household is husband, wife, and Child, people who have Family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, representation, and/or Household workers and reside in that Household.
23. Community is individuals, Families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
24. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, hereinafter abbreviated as APBD, is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of South Labuhanbatu Regency.
25. Social Rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to be able to carry out their social functions properly in Community life.

1.6.rationale: The original Indonesian regulation explicitly includes a harmful practice: child/early marriage. Pasal 38 huruf b states "mencegah terjadinya perkawinan pada usia anak-anak" (prevent marriage at child age). That is a classic harmful practice under many VAW/C frameworks. Therefore the correct label should be Yes. The judge answered No because it looked only for examples like FGM/honour crimes and missed that early marriage is present in the policy (and would have been sufficient evidence if retrieved/considered).

1.8.evaluator_rationale: While exploitation is discussed (including prostitution, forced labor, slavery-like practices), none of the passages explicitly mention human trafficking/trafficking in persons.

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by "the principle of respect for human rights" is that the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence is to guarantee the fulfillment of the rights of victims of violence as a manifestation of respect for human rights.
Letter b What is meant by "the right to life, survival, and development" are the Rights as regulated in the provisions of the 1945 Constitution.
Letter c What is meant by "Non-discriminatory" is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.
Letter d What is meant by the principle of the best interests of the Child is that in all actions concerning Children carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies, and judicial bodies, the best interests of the child must be the primary consideration.
Letter e What is meant by "the principle of Gender equality and justice" is a process of equality and conditions for men and Women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural activities, national defense and security and equality in enjoying the results of such development.
Letter f What is meant by "the principle of protection of the Rights of victims" is protection of the personal self, Family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, a sense of security and protection from threats of fear, freedom from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity.

Article 29

b. preparing reporting and referral mechanisms between regional apparatus organizations with authority over the protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence with relevant agencies and with P2TP2A; and

Article 43
(1) Community social institutions as referred to in Article 42 paragraph (2) letter d, implementing protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence must coordinate with P2TP2A.
(2) Regional Government encourages the business sector to participate in the protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence.

1.8.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, there is no clear, direct provision defining or addressing "perdagangan orang" (trafficking in persons) as a form of violence within the scope provisions. The regulation does mention trafficking only in passing as a category of women/children needing protection (e.g., Pasal 33 huruf e: "Perempuan Korban perdagangan orang"; Pasal 38 huruf h includes "Anak yang diperdagangkan" and "penjualan dan perdagangan"). However, it does not set out trafficking as a covered violence type or provide trafficking-specific prevention/response measures; the closest substantive content is "eksploitasi" (Pasal 11) which lists prostitution/forced labor/slavery-like practices but still does not explicitly state trafficking. Given the indicator is specifically "Human trafficking", the judge’s No is reasonable on the retrieved evidence and arguably on the document overall; the golden Yes appears overstated.

CHAPTER V
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

Article 27
(1) Regional Government through regional apparatus with authority over Women and Children is obligated to compile data and information regarding the protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence.
(2) Data and information as referred to in paragraph (1) includes: a. Women and Children who are Victims of acts of Violence; b. fulfillment of the rights of Women and Children;
c. Women and Children at risk or vulnerable; and
d. Women and Children who require special protection.
(3) In the management of data and information on Women and Children as referred to in paragraph (2), it is obligatory to:
a. establish a data and information system;
b. create disaggregated data;
c. conduct studies on the development of problems of Women and Children regarding acts of Violence; and
d. conduct periodic publication of data and information that can be accessed by the public.
(4) As material for the completeness of data and information as referred to in paragraph (3), regional apparatus with authority over the protection of Women and Children cooperates with and requests data from related agencies.

Article 28
(1) Data and information as referred to in Article 27 shall become material for the formulation of policies, programs, budgets, monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence.
(2) The formulation of policies, programs, budgets, monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented through the following mechanism: a. creating mapping, long-term, medium-term and short-term plans; b. creating agreements on the periodization of monthly and annual working meetings; c. creating agreements on the collection, mapping and presentation of data among regional apparatus organizations;
d. incorporating agreements into programs and budgets; and e. conducting scheduling of monitoring, evaluation and reporting.

4.2.rationale: The original Indonesian text contains prevention/education-type measures that include gender equality concepts. Pasal 21 provides prevention through "sosialisasi" of laws on women/children’s rights and "pemberdayaan dan penyadaran" (empowerment and awareness) by providing information/guidance/counseling. Separately, Pasal 33 mandates "Pengarusutamaan Gender" and includes actions like providing guidance to government apparatus for integrating gender in planning/budgeting and developing a gender-based information system. While not framed as school curriculum, these are still gender-equality information/awareness/education measures. Therefore a Yes is defensible; the golden label No likely reflects a narrower interpretation (e.g., only formal education curricula), but the policy does include gender-equality awareness/guidance provisions.
